Dealer Visits Seller's House To Buy Six Cars, Picks One for Himself
34 photos
Photo: George J Saliba | YouTube
A senior driver called a dealer and invited him to his house to sell him his car collection. He has an impressive and exclusive lineup of Porsche cars, a DeLorean, a couple of Dodge Challengers, and a Mercedes-Benz. However, things don’t go according to plan, and the dealer ends up with just one car that he is not even planning to sell.
Dealership owner George J. Saliba got a message from a senior car enthusiast who had just sold his business and was planning to downsize his car collection. He offered him a 2018 Dodge Challenger with just 61 miles, a 2016 Challenger Hellcat with 8,400 miles, a 2003 Mercedes-Benz 500 SL with 22,000 miles, and a 1982 DeLorean DMC-12 with just 600 miles.
The pack also includes two very exclusive Porsche models. Charles, the senior car enthusiast, owns a 2014 Porsche Panamera Turbo S Executive Exclusive Series with just 600 miles on the clock, and a 2011 Porsche 911 Turbo S with 4,912 miles and a manual transmission.
So George J Saliba is traveling to Pennsylvania in his Cybertruck, with the FSD on. He is planning to make an offer for all of them. One number for all cars. He is thinking that $295,000 for five of them, without the DeLorean, would make a good offer. But negotiating with Charles is like pulling teeth.
Photo: George J Saliba | YouTube When he offers $55,000 for the Panamera Executive Exclusive Series , both father and son nod their heads in disagreement. They were considering roughly $300,000 for the car, and they are not entirely wrong to do so. The Panamera Executive Exclusive is one of only 100 examples that saw the light of day after the official unveiling at the 2014 Los Angeles Auto Show.
The entire production run was sold out within 48 hours of the official announcement despite the quite hefty price. Porsche asked a starting price of $263,900. But you know, cars start losing value the moment they drive off the showroom floor, and German luxury sports models are the most unfortunate when it comes to depreciation.
Nowadays, such cars command between $80,000 and $125,000 on the used car market, depending on mileage and condition. The Panamera Turbo S Executive Exclusive Series came with Porsche's 4.8-liter twin-turbocharged V8, which pumps out 562 horsepower (570 metric horsepower) and 553 pound-feet (750 Newton meters) of torque.
That is enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 3.5 seconds and top out at 193 mph (310 kph). A dual-clutch seven-speed PDK automatic transmission puts the power down through all four corners. Porsche's first four-door rides on 20-inch Sport Classic wheels with bright yellow calipers, clamping Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes.
Photo: George J Saliba | YouTube A two-tone graduated paintwork, with the Deep Jet Black Metallic covering the upper half and Chestnut Brown Metallic on the lower section, matches the completely bespoke interior in premium Agatha Chestnut Brown leather sourced directly from the renowned Italian luxury furniture house Poltrona Frau.
But that is not the Porsche that impresses George J Saliba the most. For him, it is love at first sight when he lays his eyes on a Porsche 911 Turbo S, finished in black over a red leather interior. If it is the variant with the Mezger engine , as George says it is, then the 3.6-liter twin-turbocharged flat-six puts down 444 horsepower (450 metric horsepower) and 457 pound-feet (620 Newton meters) of torque.
This Porsche can do 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 3.9 seconds on its way to a top speed of 191 mph (307 kph). And, the best part of all, it is a car with a six-speed manual. With that spec and the stick shift, it can't get any better than this, so George is planning to fight for it. The 997.2 Turbo S never came with a manual or a Mezger engine.
" If I'm buying this car, I'm keeping it ," George says. But the owner is asking for over $200,000 for the thing. He offers $91,000 on the Demon. For the whole collection, leaving the DeLorean, the Mercedes, and the 911 out, he can offer $319,000, on top of the $185,000 that he is willing to pay for the 911. The owner says he needs to think. He wants auction prices for his cars without having to go through the actual auction, so he lets George leave empty-handed and waiting for his call.
Photo: George J Saliba | YouTube Days later, George calls first because he is anxious to know if he can make that black 2011 Porsche. 911 Turbo S with a red interior, his own. But the owner is well aware that he wants it badly, so he sets a prohibitive price for the car. He is asking $250,000 for it alone. They eventually close the deal for the 911 only at $220,000. But the other cars remain in the owner's garage. A very demanding owner.
He checks with Grok and raises his fist in the air. Cars like that can hit $300,000 at auctions. However, he plans to keep it. So it is a good deal after all, even if he had to stretch far more than he originally planned. He isn't even sure if the car runs and drives.
The good news is that the engine fires up with no hesitation whatsoever, so on his way back to the dealership, the new owner drives the Porsche and leaves his cameraman with the Cybertruck.
